```{r setup}

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(broom)

```

## Wrangling, cleaning, merging

```{r}
{r}
# identification data
data_id <- read_csv(here("PS1", "data_stress.csv")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  select(id, trial, screen, response, audio) %>%
  filter(screen == "response") %>%
  mutate(audio = str_remove_all(audio, ".mp3")) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(
    audio,
    delim = "_",
    names = c("talker", "talkerid", "tense", "type", "verb", "sentence")
  ) %>%
  select(-talkerid) %>%
  rename(verb_conjugation = verb) %>%
  mutate(response = stringi::stri_trans_general(response, "Latin-ASCII"))
# answer sheet
data_answers <- read_csv(here("PS1", "data_answers.csv")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  rename(verb = target_verb,
         vowel = stem_vowel)
# merge
data_id <- merge(data_id, 
                 data_answers %>% dplyr::select(sentence, tense, verb, subject, answer), 
                 by = c("sentence", "tense"))
# add proficiency data
data_proficiency <- read_csv(here("PS1", "data_proficiency.csv")) %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(tag == "click") %>%
  dplyr::select(id, answer, response) %>%
  mutate(score = ifelse(response == answer, 1, 0)) %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarize(proficiency = mean(score, na.rm = T))
# merge
data_id <- merge(data_id, data_proficiency, by = "id")
# make outcome
data_id <- data_id %>%
  mutate(score = ifelse(response == answer, 1, 0))

# remove clutter
rm(data_answers, data_proficiency)

# sanity check
# number of trials per participant
data_id %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  count() # a few got cut, but we have 79 or 80 for each individual
# normally, would go recover those trials and diagnose the issue, but for now will move on

# create summary data (one score per item type per participant)
data_summary <- data_id %>%
  group_by(id, type, proficiency) %>% # including proficiency here so that it's retained
  summarize(
    score = mean(score, na.rm = T)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Visualization

```{r}
# score by item type
ggplot(data_summary, aes(type, score)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Trial Type",
       y = "Accuracy")
# participants performed worse on targets than on fillers (distractors)

# proficiency and score
ggplot(data_summary, aes(proficiency, score)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "white") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Proficiency",
       y = "Accuracy")
# the higher the participant's proficiency, the better they performed

# both together
ggplot(data_summary, aes(proficiency, score, fill = type)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Proficiency",
       y = "Accuracy")
# alternative (separate panels)
ggplot(data_summary, aes(proficiency, score, fill = type)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Proficiency",
       y = "Accuracy") +
  facet_wrap(~ type)
```

## Analysis

```{r}
# reference level for type = filler
# intercept represents predicted performance on fillers when proficiency = 0
lm(score ~ proficiency + type, data_summary) %>%
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )

# better model (contrast-coding for type, z-scoring proficiency)
data_summary <- data_summary %>%
  mutate(
    type_contrast = ifelse(type == "filler", -0.5, 0.5),
    proficiency_z = scale(proficiency)
  )

# refit
# intercept represents grand mean (performance on both filled and target)
# type_contrast represents the difference
# proficiency represents change expressed as 1 sd
lm(score ~ proficiency_z + type_contrast, data_summary) %>%
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
```
